'''Software-defined radio (SDR)''' moves functions such as modulation, filtering, synchronization, and demodulation from fixed radio hardware into software. A configurable RF front end still converts between radio-frequency signals and digital samples.

__TOC__

== Overview ==

A typical SDR separates the radio into a configurable hardware path and an application running on a host computer.

<pre>
Receive: RF input -> RF front end -> ADC -> FPGA -> host interface -> application
Transmit: Application -> host interface -> FPGA -> DAC -> RF front end -> RF output
</pre>

The usable frequency range, bandwidth, and sample rate depend on the complete path. The RF front end, converters, FPGA configuration, host connection, and signal-processing workload must all support the selected operating point.

== Hardware ==

=== NI USRP-2954R ===

The [[NI USRP-2954R]] is the documented IHF platform for wideband SDR work in the 10 MHz to 6 GHz range. The installed unit has two UBX-160 daughterboards and a dual-10-Gigabit-Ethernet host connection. Its hardware page contains the connector mapping, network setup, startup checks, and RF limits.

==== Project on this hardware ====

The [[OFDM-based Joint Communication and Sensing (JCAS)|OFDM-based Joint Communication and Sensing project]] uses the USRP-2954R to develop a shared OFDM waveform for data transmission and environmental sensing.

== Software ==

The current USRP workflow uses:

* '''UHD''' to discover, configure, and stream samples to and from the USRP;
* '''GNU Radio''' to assemble and run signal-processing flowgraphs;
* '''Python''' for custom GNU Radio blocks, automation, and visualisation; and
* '''Git''' for version-controlled development. See [[GIT - Versionskontrolle]].

Device-specific setup belongs on the hardware page. Algorithms, parameters, results, and source-code instructions belong on the relevant project page or in its repository.

== General RF practice ==

* Check the frequency, power, impedance, and connector ratings of every component before making a connection.
* Use suitable attenuation and 50-ohm terminations for conducted measurements.
* Disable RF outputs before changing cables or instruments.
* Never exceed the input limit of an SDR or measurement instrument.
* Record hardware identifiers, software versions, clock and sample rates, centre frequency, gain, bandwidth, connector mapping, and runtime warnings with every measurement.
